questions.stem: The civil service is best described as the

options.text: body of elected legislators who make the law
body of permanent officials who advise on and implement government policy
association of workers that calls nationwide strikes
council of traditional rulers in a state

questions.explanation: Civil servants are career officials, not elected politicians. They brief ministers, draft instruments, keep records and carry out approved policy. Legislators, labour unions and traditional councils perform different roles.

distractorRationale.a: Elected legislators constitute the legislature, not the civil service
distractorRationale.c: A striking workers' association is a pressure group such as the NLC
distractorRationale.d: Traditional rulers belong to customary institutions, not the civil service

questions.stem: Anonymity in the civil service means that civil servants

options.text: must resign whenever a new party wins an election
are not publicly identified as the authors of government policy
may campaign for the ruling party while in office
are elected by the staff of their ministry

questions.explanation: The minister is the public face of the ministry; the official who drafted the memo is not named in the press conference or the National Assembly hearing. Anonymity protects the official's ability to serve the next government, and it keeps political responsibility where it belongs — on the elected or appointed politician.

distractorRationale.a: Resigning with a change of government would violate permanence, not describe anonymity
distractorRationale.c: Campaigning for a party would violate neutrality
distractorRationale.d: Civil servants are appointed, not elected by colleagues

questions.stem: The principle of permanence in the civil service is illustrated when

options.text: a permanent secretary remains in office after a change of ruling party
a minister is re-appointed by a new President
a civil servant is elected to the Senate
a ministry is named after the President in power

questions.explanation: Permanence means the administrative machinery outlives the political executive. The permanent secretary is a career official; the minister is not. Continuity of files, contracts and institutional memory depends on that difference.

distractorRationale.b: A minister is a political appointee and does not illustrate the permanence of the service
distractorRationale.c: Election to the Senate takes the person out of the civil service into the legislature
distractorRationale.d: Renaming a ministry is a political act, not a feature of the service

questions.stem: NEPA (later PHCN) and NITEL are examples of Nigerian

options.text: civil service ministries
public corporations
political parties
local government councils

questions.explanation: Both were statutory bodies created to provide a commercial public utility — electricity and telecommunications — rather than ordinary ministerial departments. Their later unbundling and sale are the usual Nigerian illustrations of privatisation of public corporations.

distractorRationale.a: A ministry such as Power or Communications is a government department, not the utility corporation itself
distractorRationale.d: Local government councils are the third tier of government, not national utilities

questions.stem: A major reason for the privatisation of public corporations in Nigeria was to

options.text: increase the number of political appointees in each corporation
reduce inefficiency, corruption and the fiscal burden of loss-making state enterprises
abolish the civil service and replace it with private clerks
transfer the National Assembly's law-making power to company boards

questions.explanation: From the Structural Adjustment Programme of 1986 and the 1988 privatisation decree onwards, successive governments argued that corporations such as NEPA/PHCN, NITEL and Nigeria Airways were overstaffed, politically interfered with and dependent on subvention. Sale or commercialisation was meant to impose market discipline and free public funds. Whether those aims were fully met is debated; the stated reason remains efficiency and reduced fiscal burden.

distractorRationale.a: Privatisation is intended to reduce, not increase, political patronage in commercial operations
distractorRationale.c: The civil service is a separate institution and was not abolished by privatisation
distractorRationale.d: Law making remains with the legislature; company boards do not inherit it

questions.stem: Neutrality requires a civil servant to resign when a party he or she privately supports loses a general election.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: False. Neutrality means the official serves whichever party wins, without using the office to help or harm it. Combined with permanence, it is precisely why the official does not resign. Private voting remains free; public partisanship in office does not.

distractorRationale.a: Resigning after a defeat would collapse the service after every election and confuse neutrality with party membership
